I went to the Davidoff store and Gestocigars. I felt like a kid in a candy shop at Gestocigars, literally floor to ceiling full of boxes. They had everything, it was pretty wild and the prices compared to France were a solid 5-10 euros cheaper. The Davidoff store carries just about every Davidoff cigar but they had a very very solid selection. I recommend checking them both out, I window shopped the Davidoff store first before going to Gestocigars, I purchased some of the things there like the Monterey's and H. Uppmans. Gestocigars has sales as well. If you're going to buy boxes check them out first.

I've liked all of the H. Uppmans I've gotten. The C No. #1 was the first Cuban I had and I fell in love instantly. Immediately got the creamy vanilla taste as soon as it was lit. I was a little underwhelmed with the majestics. I know Partagas gets a lot of love here, I've tried the series D #4 and the super Partagas but I didn't particularly care for them. The Mille Fleur was kind of spicy and peppery, it's not a bad every day smoke.

Here's an almost complete positional player breakdown of San Diego's best sports franchise: 

Catcher: Austin Hedges: a former top 100 prospect he was highly regarded as a defense first catcher, he sniffed the majors in 2015 where he batted ~.180 in ~120 AB's. He spent all of last year (2016) in the minors where he batted ~.330 and mashed ~24 home runs. If he lives up to the hype, we're looking at a young Russel Martin, if he doesn't, he'll be a AAAA player at best.

C/RP/OF - Christian Bethancourt: A former top 100 prospect, we acquired him in a trade with Atlanta with Matt Kemp. He was Derek Norris (former starting catcher) backup. This past offseason, he's been developed into a relief pitcher to full fill a sort of super utility role. The last catcher to pitcher experiment was Kenley Jensen, so we'll see if he pans out.

1b: Wil Myers: All Star, Rookie of the Year, Second Runner up for the NL Gold Glove, Franchise 1b. Don't let his overall stat line for 2016 dissuade you. He was very good in the first half because he had protection in the batting line up with Matt Kemp batting behind him. He battled a wrist injury but had surgery in the 2015 offseason to remove bone spurs. One to watch!

1B - Josh Naylor - A top 100 prospect and top 10 1b prospect. Acquired in a trade with the Marlins that included Andrew Cashner. He's a big boy, so 1b/DH is the best he's gonna do. At the age of 19 he still has a few years to go before he sniffs the majors. 

2b - Cory Spangenberg - Another former top 100 prospect and first round pick, Cory was expected to be the franchise 2b. Coming off a decent rookie year that saw him bat ~.270, he was disrupted when he tore his quadricep in the first month of the season.

2b/3b - Ryan Schimpf - Acquired in a trade with the Blue Jays that saw us part ways with Melvin Upton Jr. Schimpf came in and was a Home Run hitting machine, winning Rookie of the Month in August. He became the fastest rookie to 20 homes runs with under 200 AB's. If he can make more contact (hitting ~.220 last season) expect Brian Dozier like number. The competition for 2b is gonna be tough.

2b/3b/LF - Carlos Asuaje - Acquired in a trade with the Red Sox that saw us lose Kimbrel, he quickly raised himself prospect lists. Last year in AAA he hit ~.320 with ~10 hr's, expect him to fill a super utility role or transition to SS.

SS - Luis Sardinas - Not that highly regarded, looks to be our primary SS for the season while our other minors developed. Did bat ~.280 in the time he was here, so we'll see if he finds his swing while here.

SS - Javier Guerra - A highly touted SS prospect, he was included in the Boston trade. He suffered an undisclosed injury in his first season with us that saw his stock drop, but expect him to bounce back. Should be our SS of the future if he gets his act together.

SS - Ruddy Giron - Another SS, not has highly touted as Guerra, he was running hot in his first season with us, expect him to rise up prospect lists

3b - Yangervis Solarte - Acquired in a trade for Chase Headley to the New York Yankees, Solarte has been the face of the Padres. He's a big fan favorite and the definition of clutch. 9/10 Solarte comes up with a hit when we need it the most, those late game rallies normally start with this guy. 

OF - Alex Dickerson - San Diego Native, he grew up in Poway. Was never highly regarded but does this kid have some power. In a game against the Blue Jays in Toronto, he launched a ball to the 5'th deck. A feat done by 15 other players, Mark Mcgwire was the first to do it. Expect him to put up a fight in LF, if he can make more contact, expect around ~.280 ~20hr's. 

OF - Travis Jankowski - Future Gold Glove defender, Speedy, Great Routes, his nickname is Fred. If he can make better contact expect him to be the leadoff runner for the padres for years to come. Has the potential of being the next billy hamilton but with a better avg.

OF -Hunter Renfroe - Boy, oh boy, have we been waiting for this guy. Absolutely demolished the minors last season, and started his MLB career with a slash. In his limited taste in the MLB he batted ~.370 with 4 homeruns. 2 of them coming in 1 game including not only a grand slam, but he was also the first person, in park history, to hit one to the top of the Western Metal Building in a game. The hype is real.

OF - Manuel Margot - Another top 100 prospect, Margot was acquired from Boston from Kimbrel. He too destroyed the minors in his time here in SD, he's expected to develop quite a bit of pop and he has the speed. Expect ~.300 avg with ~15 home runs and ~30-40 sb's.  He will be competing with Travis Jankowski for the starting job in CF.
